text:
kevin: thinking out loud — we need a single bench protocol that lets us compare kernel-selection changes, batching heuristics, and KV-cache behavior without noise. current runs feel inconsistent. any thoughts on defining an 'apples-to-apples' harness?

maria: agree. two pillars: deterministic input set + controlled cache state. replay traces for representativeness, synthetic traffic for repeatability. both are needed.

sam: profiling from yesterday shows a regression after the new fused-softmax kernel landed — p99 for 2k seq shots up 18% on node A. attaching high-level notes below (will post traces to gcs).

kevin: that's the problem — we can't tell if it's kernel selection logic or batching changes. suggestion: force a single kernel during a run as an A/B and compare.

jordan: metrics recap so we're consistent: TTFT = time from request received by runtime to first token emitted (server-side). TPOT = time per output token measured as median token-emission interval after first token. goodput = tokens emitted that meet the latency SLO (e.g. tokens/sec where TTFT < SLO). QPS = requests/sec regardless of token counts. p95/p99 applied to TTFT and TPOT separately.

rachel: question: how do we handle KV cache warm/cold? replay traces usually warm caches which hides cold-start costs.

maria: plan: run each experiment in three phases — cold (empty KV), warmup (feed a fixed prompt set to stabilize caches), steady-state (measure). report metrics separately by phase. also include cache hit ratio and avg KV lookup latency.

kevin: +1. also we should fix model flags: quantization level, kernel prefs, workspace sizes, GPU power settings. document the hardware and driver versions in the run metadata.

sam: here are quick profiling highlights from the regression run: top hotspots: attention kernel (42%), KV gather (19%), softmax (12%), alloc/free churn (9%). timeline shows a spike at kernel selection switch.

jordan: sounds like kernel-selection heuristics are picking a new kernel for certain seq-len buckets. we should log kernel decisions per request so we can correlate with latency spikes.

kevin: agreed. instrumenting decision points is cheap and extremely useful. bench-bot — can we add kernel-choice logging to perf payloads?

bench-bot: noted. adding `kernel_choice` field to perf records and histograms. next run will include it. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: quick run summary (1774005690): synthetic loadgen 8 workers, poisson arrival lambda=5r/s, seq_len=1024/256 mix 70/30, batch_policy=random up to 8, model pinned v1.9-q4. p95 TTFT=84ms, p99 TTFT=162ms. logs at gs://redwood-perf/1774005678/run-1/*

rachel: synthetic looks fine but we need a replay harness variant that preserves concurrency profile. replay the trace scaled to the same mean concurrency and preserve inter-arrival times. otherwise throughput isn't comparable.

maria: agreed. also define warmup duration: either fixed number of requests (e.g. 10k) or until KV hit ratio stabilizes within +/-1% for 1 minute. pick whichever occurs first.

jordan: about aggregation windows: publish both short-window percentiles (1m sliding) and run-level percentiles. short windows help catch sporadic jitter from kernel switches.

sam: for A/B kernel experiments: run N repeats (N>=5) per variant, shuffle order to avoid time-of-day confounds. report median across repeats and show scatter.

kevin: good. run orchestration checklist for each experiment: 1) lock model version/flags 2) clear KV or run warmup 3) fixed load profile (seeded PRNG) 4) enable kernel_choice logging 5) collect CPU/GPU traces + perf records 6) publish raw and aggregated metrics.

devex: I'll draft a short run config template and add to the docs. sample loadgen config:```json
{
  "mode": "synthetic",
  "workers": 8,
  "arrival_dist": "poisson",
  "lambda": 5,
  "seq_mix": [{"len":1024,"pct":70},{"len":256,"pct":30}],
  "batch_policy": "random",
  "max_batch":8,
  "seed": 42
}
```

rachel: nice. also include a replay config snippet that maps trace time to scaled wallclock and preserves inter-arrival windows.

kevin: one last: goodput vs QPS confusion — we should include both in dashboards. goodput tells product teams cost-effective throughput; QPS helps capacity planning. label them clearly.

maria: action items: (1) bench-bot: add kernel_choice field and cache metrics; (2) devex: add config template and run checklist; (3) infra: schedule nightly synthetic regression and weekly replay runs; (4) sam/jordan: investigate fused-softmax regression with kernel pinned runs.

sam: will start with pinned-kernel runs today and post traces.

bench-bot: tasks created: #B-1423 (kernel_choice logs), #B-1424 (cache metrics).

kevin: thanks all — if we stick to this protocol we'll get reproducible apples-to-apples comparisons and faster regression triage. :thumbsup:
